name: Do I need a permit to replace a bathtub in San Diego County?

mainEntity.name: Do I need a permit to replace a bathtub in San Diego County?

acceptedAnswer.text:
Permit requirements depend on the exact work and property. In the City of San Diego, official guidance lists tub-to-tub and shower-to-shower replacements that do not change size or location among work that may qualify for a no-plan permit pathway, while other plumbing or alteration work can require permits.

Context: Historic resources, designated districts, structural changes, added fixtures, relocated plumbing, and work beyond a like-for-like replacement may change the review path. Rules can also differ outside the City of San Diego, including Chula Vista, Coronado, National City, and Imperial Beach.

Key factors:
- Whether size or location changes
- Plumbing, electrical, structural, or wall alterations
- Property location and historic status
- Who will obtain and close permits

Practical guidance: Ask for the applicable permit approach in writing before demolition and confirm whether inspections and final documentation are included. Do not assume a quote’s statement that permits are unnecessary applies to every part of the project.

Elite Remodeling & Design’s published process includes coordinating permit applications when the project scope calls for them.
acceptedAnswer.description: It depends on the scope and jurisdiction. City of San Diego guidance identifies some same-size, same-location tub replacements as eligible for a no-plan pathway, while relocated plumbing, structural changes, added fixtures, historic conditions, or broader remodeling can change the requirements. Confirm locally before work begins.
